name: Readout-dependent empirical sample scaling, frame_scaling

downstream_annotations.scheme: Every downstream position h>=2 is independently observed with probability pi. The observation is U_h=C_h*independent_noise(mu), the selected VALUE sign. Missingness uniforms and noise are shared across pi conditions for pairing, independent across examples/positions and independent of inputs/final noise. The posterior m_h=b_h if unobserved, else (b_h+mu*U_h)/(1+mu*U_h*b_h); when |b_h|=1, m_h=b_h. Use partial_1 G(m) as weight. Exact effective kappa1=sum_{A contains1}hat_g(A)^2*r^(|A|-1), r=(1+pi*mu^2)/2. Binary posterior has five possible values, so a five-level exact multilinear lookup is used.

model: Exact shared-frame Gaussian hard retrieval, maximum depth nine, binary candidates, q uniform on S^(d-1), ambient value axis coordinate zero, frame in its orthogonal complement. Full Gaussian records and all nine recursive selection steps are generated. Conditions share observations and final-noise signs within seed. Training final labels are noisy public readouts of selected value SIGNS; no indices or intermediate labels enter final-derivative estimators.
noise: Independent final and first-value noise signs, each P(+1)=0.9, independent of all data. Final noise is shared across readouts only for pairing.
random_readouts: For each specified truth seed, PCG64 permutes a vector with exactly half -1 and half +1 entries. Bit coordinate j is bit j of row index, 0 means -1. Truth tables are publicly fixed before target/training seeds and saved in full. One random function per selected depth, not an ensemble claim.
estimator: For every readout g, D1=partial_1 G(b) is computed exactly using a public ternary lookup, b_h=(sign(g_h0)+sign(g_h1))/2. Average Y*D1*R1*q^T, R1=sum_i g_1i*(z_1i-zbar_1). Thin-SVD polar produces the frame without target alignment. Same-count auxiliary comparator averages noisy first selected VALUE*R1*q^T. All singular values and rank-deficient completions retained.
fourier: Compute every Fourier coefficient by exact finite Walsh transform; beta=sum_A hat_g(A)^2*2^-|A|, kappa1=sum_A containing1 hat_g(A)^2*2^(1-|A|). Quantities never determine sample sizes or outcomes.
primary_metric: Oriented frame error ||P_hat-P||F/sqrt(d), no Procrustes rotation. Threshold fixed at0.35. For each seed/readout, first observed grid size below threshold defines the crossing. Record preceding/current grid bracket; left/right censoring retained. Full fixed grid is always run, even after crossing.
secondary_metric: Interpolate log(error) linearly against log(n) between the two observed crossing endpoints; do not extrapolate censored observations. Also report the raw discrete first-crossing count and all errors. Threshold is an evaluation criterion, not used to choose a deployed checkpoint.
plots: Headline panel A: log2 observed interpolated crossing count vs -log2(beta) for unannotated readouts. Panel B: same unadjusted count vs -log2(kappa1), with annotation conditions at their effective kappa1. The first-value common-count reference is shown. A separate normalized plot n*kappa1 vs readout shows the estimator's pivot factor transparently. Censored points arrows, counts explicit. Distinct family colors and all seed points retained; no beta-based rescaling of the observed sample count.
regression: Descriptive OLS over readout-level means of log2 interpolated crossing count, complete-case only with censoring counts explicit. Pair bootstrap the twelve independent repetitions,10000 resamples using fixed seed20261021, to quantify seed variation. Families and functions are fixed, so intervals do not quantify uncertainty over possible readout families or prove an asymptotic exponent. No claim about SGD or an information-theoretic lower bound follows from this experiment.
uncertainty: Pointwise95% Student-t intervals over twelve independent target/data repetitions; df11 t=2.200985160082949. Plot log-count intervals on log scale. All reported outcomes retained, including unfavorable/censored and rank-deficient cases.
reproducibility: PCG64 with SeedSequence([seed,stream]), float64. Freeze source and protocol SHA256 before execution; refuse overwrite. Save all target frames, truth tables/coefficients/derivative tables, moment estimates and fitted frames at all sample counts, independent test inputs/predictions, first64 raw examples, each generation-block RNG state, environment/timing, and output hashes. All training observations can be regenerated; not every training observation is duplicated in storage. Existing fixed_budget files are immutable.
